text.tspan: Error minus B0's at the plant
(percentage points of capacity)

text.aria-label: Title text 'Lead-day 1 is the forecast for the day after the day it is issued. AN is the arm the screening rule picked from the first 10 months. All rows are exploratory. Arms. AN: the analogue ensemble: the mean, clear-sky index and spread of the power, rescaled by clear-sky irradiance, on the 5 of the last 30 days whose forecast clear-sky index was closest to the target's. PC: the 7-day ratio of power to CAMS satellite irradiance, and the 30-day ratio of CAMS to forecast irradiance. W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same hour over the last 7 whole days. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. TF: the 30-day ratio of power to forecast irradiance (the transfer ratio). B0: the baseline with no lag. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). N1: a random day 8 to 28 days earlier (keeps the plant's slowly changing output level). N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control). IM: the morning's power on the forecast day. T1: days since the record began. Month-block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use. KS: all of L1, IM, W7, Q30, TF, S3, and RP together. L2: L1 plus that hour's weather forecast. RP: the plant's recent energy relative to the other plants. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its residual at the lag hour. CK: the plant's clipping ceiling. CTX7: seven separate daily lags and their weather forecasts. S3: a two-step forecast that adds the first-stage forecast's mean residual over the last 1, 7, and 30 days.'
text.tspan: Lead-day 1 is the forecast for the day after the day it is issued. AN is the arm the screening rule picked from the first 10
months.
All rows are exploratory.
Arms. AN: the analogue ensemble: the mean, clear-sky index and spread of the power, rescaled by clear-sky irradiance, on the
5 of the last 30 days whose forecast clear-sky index was closest to the target's. PC: the 7-day ratio of power to CAMS
satellite irradiance, and the 30-day ratio of CAMS to forecast irradiance. W7: the minimum, maximum, and mean of the same
hour over the last 7 whole days. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of the same hour. TF: the 30-day ratio of power
to forecast irradiance (the transfer ratio). B0: the baseline with no lag. L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the
latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). N1: a random day 8
to 28 days earlier (keeps the plant's slowly changing output level). N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null
control). IM: the morning's power on the forecast day. T1: days since the record began. Month-block folds interleave, so
trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a
live forecast could use. KS: all of L1, IM, W7, Q30, TF, S3, and RP together. L2: L1 plus that hour's weather forecast. RP:
the plant's recent energy relative to the other plants. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its
residual at the lag hour. CK: the plant's clipping ceiling. CTX7: seven separate daily lags and their weather forecasts. S3:
a two-step forecast that adds the first-stage forecast's mean residual over the last 1, 7, and 30 days.
